hero_headline: Trusted Land Services for Oil & Gas, Minerals & Renewables
hero_subheadline: Certified Professional Landmen handling title research, lease acquisition, due diligence, and renewable energy land work for operators, producers, mineral owners, and investors.
value_paragraph:
Every file is worked start to finish by a Certified Professional Landman. There is no junior staff and no handoff between the person doing the research and the person reporting it.

Deliverables state what the record shows, what it does not, and where the exposure sits.
regions_note: Select a basin or a highlighted state to see the plays worked there. Shaded states mark completed project experience; we take on work nationwide.

regions.name: Gulf Coast Basin
regions.summary: Primary working area for the firm. Deep gas development in the Haynesville and Bossier, oil in the Tuscaloosa Marine Shale, and long-established conventional production along the coast. Salt-dome geology and fragmented ownership are common.

plays.name: Haynesville Shale
plays.definition: A deep, high-pressure dry gas play across northwest Louisiana and East Texas, and one of the largest gas producers in the country.

plays.name: Bossier
plays.definition: A gas-bearing interval stacked above the Haynesville, frequently developed alongside it in East Texas and North Louisiana.

plays.name: Tuscaloosa Marine Shale
plays.definition: An oil-prone shale running across central Louisiana and southwest Mississippi, commonly abbreviated TMS.

plays.name: Eagle Ford Shale
plays.definition: A South Texas oil, condensate, and gas play running in a band from the Mexican border northeast toward East Texas.

plays.name: East Texas Basin
plays.definition: A long-producing conventional basin, home to the historic East Texas Oil Field and multiple stacked targets still developed today.

plays.name: Gulf Coast Trend
plays.definition: The onshore coastal belt across Texas, Louisiana, and Mississippi, where shallow conventional production and salt-dome structures dominate.

regions.name: Permian Basin
regions.summary: The largest oil-producing basin in the United States, covering more than 75,000 square miles across West Texas and southeast New Mexico. Stacked pay in the Midland and Delaware sub-basins makes depth severance and multi-horizon ownership routine title issues.

plays.name: Midland Sub-basin
plays.definition: The eastern half of the Permian, where the Spraberry and Wolfcamp benches are developed in tight, heavily leased sections.

plays.name: Delaware Sub-basin
plays.definition: The deeper western half of the Permian, running into southeast New Mexico with thicker Bone Spring and Wolfcamp targets.

regions.name: Appalachian Basin
regions.summary: Stacked Marcellus and Utica development over some of the oldest and most fragmented mineral title in the country. Heirship research, record gaps, and century-old severances are common here.

plays.name: Marcellus Shale
plays.definition: The largest natural gas field in the United States, centered in Pennsylvania and West Virginia.

plays.name: Utica Shale
plays.definition: A deeper play lying beneath the Marcellus, productive for gas, condensate, and oil, particularly in eastern Ohio.

plays.name: Clinton / Medina
plays.definition: Shallow conventional sandstones across eastern Ohio and western Pennsylvania with more than a century of production history.

plays.name: Chattanooga Shale
plays.definition: A Devonian shale across Tennessee and the southern Appalachians, developed both conventionally and unconventionally.

regions.name: Michigan Basin
regions.summary: A circular intracratonic basin centered on the Lower Peninsula, producing from multiple stacked horizons. Shallow biogenic gas here was among the earliest commercial shale development in the country.

plays.name: Antrim Shale
plays.definition: A shallow biogenic gas play in the northern Michigan Basin, and one of the first commercially developed shale gas plays in the United States.

plays.name: Northern Michigan Conventional
plays.definition: Niagaran reef and Trenton-Black River targets developed across the northern Lower Peninsula.

regions.name: Pacific Northwest
regions.summary: Renewable energy land work. Utility-scale solar and wind siting involves surface use agreements, setbacks, and long-term option periods, along with transmission and interconnection right-of-way.

plays.name: Solar & Wind Lease Acquisition
plays.definition: Option and lease packages assembled across contiguous surface tracts for utility-scale renewable siting.

plays.name: Right-of-Way Corridors
plays.definition: Transmission and interconnection routing, negotiated tract by tract to connect generation to the grid.
